3300.full: 1. to modulate, sing, warble , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): mostly in Mid., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

s: to give a share of, impart
3301.lxx: in LXX: Pro.11:29 (שָׁבַר hi.), Wis.7:13, al.

3302.lxx: in LXX: Deu.19:14 (סוּג hi.), Isa.54:10 (מוֹט), etc.
3302.full: μετα-κινέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Deu.19:14 (סוּג hi.), Isa.54:10 (מוֹט), etc. ;] trans., to move away, remove (ὅρια, Deu, l.with). Mid., to remove oneself, remove, shift: metaphorically, ἀπὸ τ. ἐλπίδος, Col.1:23.† (AS)

3304.lxx: in LXX: Exo.16:18, Num.35:5, Rut.3:15, Isa.40:12, (מָדַד), Da Th Dan.5:26 (מָדַד), Wis.4:8 *
3304.full: μετρέω, -ῶ (μέτρον), [in LXX: Exo.16:18, Num.35:5, Rut.3:15, Isa.40:12, (מָדַד), Da Th Dan.5:26 (מָדַד), Wis.4:8 * ;] __1. to measure, of space, number, value, etc.: with accusative of thing(s), Rev.11:2 21:15, 17; with dative instr., Rev.11:1 21:16. Metaphorical, ἑαυτὸν ἐν ἑαυτῷ, 2Co.10:12. __2. to measure out, give by measure: prov., ἐν ὧ μέτρῳ κ.τ.λ., Mat.7:2, Mrk.4:24, Luk.6:38 (WH, mg., cf. ἀντι-μετρέω).† (AS)

3305.full: 1. an adulteress , (New Testament):as adjective adulterous , (New Testament) 2. as Substantive = μοιχεία, (New Testament) (ML)

3306.full: μονογενής, -ές (μόνος, γένος), [in LXX: Jdg.11:34, Psa.22:20 25:16 35:17 (יָחִיד), Tob.3:15 6:10, 14 8:17, Wis.7:22, Bar.4:16 * ;] only, only begotten (DCG, ii, 281), of sons and daughters : Luk.7:12 8:42 9:38, Heb.11:17; of Christ, Jhn.3:16, 18, 1Jn.4:9; μ. παρὰ πατρός, Jhn.1:14; μ. θεός, Jhn.1:18.† (AS)

3309.full: a fly , Lat. musca, (Iliad by Homer):—;proverbial, μυίης θάρσος, of excessive boldness, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

3311.full: fit for battle, warlike , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἱ μ. the fighting men, soldiery , and in Egypt the warrior-caste , (Herdotus Historicus); τὸ μ. the effective force , (Thucydides) (ML)

3312.full: 1. a bee , Lat. apis, (Homer), etc. 2. one of the priestesses of Delphi, (Pindar) 3. = μέλι, honey , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

3313.lxx: in LXX: Psa.55:22 (יְהַב), Job.11:18, Sir.30:24, al
3313.full: μέριμνα, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: Psa.55:22 (יְהַב), Job.11:18, Sir.30:24, al ;] (in cl. chiefly poët.) care, anxiety: 1Pe.5:7; pl., Luk.8:14 21:34; with genitive obj., Mat.13:22, Mrk.4:19, 2Co.11:28.† (AS)

3314.full: μίασμα, -τος, τό (μιαίνω), chiefly in trag. and late writers; [in LXX: Lev.7:8, 18, (פִּגּוּל), Jer.32:34 (שִׁקּוּץ), Eze.33:31 (בֶּצַע), Jdth.9:2, 4 13:16, 1Ma.13:50 * ;] a stain, defilement: pl., 2Pe.2:20.† (AS)

3315.full: a wooded vale, dell , or glen , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

s: to wash, usually of a part of the body
3316.full: νίπτω late form of νίζω, [in LXX chiefly for רָחַץ ;] to wash, usually of a part of the body: with accusative of person(s), Jhn.13:8; τ. πόδας, Jhn.13:5-6, 8 13:12, 14, 1Ti.5:10; mid., reflexive, to wash oneself: Jhn.9:7, 11 9:15; τ. χεῖρας, Mat.15:2, Mrk.7:3; τ. πόδας, Jhn.13:10; τ. πρόσωπον, Mat.6:17 (in cl. Att.. prose, used only in compounds; cf. ἀπο-νίπτω).† νίζω, see: νίπτω SYN.: λούω (which see), πλύνω (AS)

3317.full: divination by the flight or cries of birds , Lat. augurium, (Euripides) (ML)

3319.full: οὐρά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX for זָנָב ;] a tail: Rev.9:10, 19 12:4.† (AS)

3321.lxx: in LXX: Jos.9:4, Pro.1:4 8:5 (עׇרְמָה), Num.24:22, Sir.19:25 21:22 31:10 (Sir.34:10) (in all cases in good or  indifferent sense)*
3321.full: πανουργία, -ας, ἡ (πανοῦργος), [in LXX: Jos.9:4, Pro.1:4 8:5 (עׇרְמָה), Num.24:22, Sir.19:25 21:22 31:10 (Sir.34:10) (in all cases in good or indifferent sense)* ;] cleverness, in cl. nearly always in bad sense, craftiness, cunning, knavery: Luk.20:23, 1Co.3:19 (LXX, φρόνησις, for עׇרְמָה) 2Co.4:2 11:3, Eph.4:14.† (AS)

3322.full: παρα-βιάζομαι [in LXX: Gen.19:9, 4Ki.2:17 (פָּצַר), Deu.1:43 (זוּד hi.), 1Ki.28:23 (פָּרַץ) see1. 4 * ;] __1. prop., to force against nature or law. __2. to compel by force (Polyb.). __3. to constrain by entreaty (Ge, 1Sam, ll. with): Luk.24:29, Act.16:15.† (AS)

3323.full: to do an incredible thing; render notorious

s: to hear without heeding, take no heed
3325.lxx: in LXX: Est.3:3, 8 (עָבַר, עָשָׂה, with neg.) Est.4:14 7:4 (חָרַשׁ hi.), Isa.65:12 (שָׁמַע, with neg.), I Est.4:11, Tob.3:4 *
3325.full: παρ-ακούω [in LXX: Est.3:3, 8 (עָבַר, עָשָׂה, with neg.) Est.4:14 7:4 (חָרַשׁ hi.), Isa.65:12 (שָׁמַע, with neg.), I Est.4:11, Tob.3:4 * ;] __1. to overhear. __2. to hear amiss or imperfectly. __3. Later (as in LXX, Polyb., Plut.; also in π., see MM, xviii), to hear without heeding, take no heed: Mrk.5:36; with genitive, Mat.18:17.† (AS)

3326.full: παρα-πίπτω [in LXX: Eze.14:13 15:8 18:24 20:27 (מָעַל), Eze.22:4 (אָשַׁם), Est.6:10 (נָפַל hi.), Wis.6:9 12:2, 2Ma.10:4 A* ;] __1. most frequently (Hdt., Thuc., al.), to fall in one's way, befall. __2. to fall into or in (before εἰς, Polyb.; with dative, 2Mac, l.with). __3. to fall away (En, Wis, ll. with; in Polyb., with genitive) : absol., Heb.6:6. __4. to fail (λόγος, Es, l.with; cf. 1Ki.3:19).† (AS)

3327.full: marks of virginity; tokens of virginity

3328.full: πατριάρχης, -ου, ὁ (πατριά, ἄρχω), [in LXX: 1Ch.24:31 (אָב), 2Ch.19:8 26:12 (אָב רֹאשׁ), 1Ch.27:12 (שַׂר), 2Ch.23:20 (מֵאָה שַׂר), 4Ma.7:19 4Mac 16:25 * ;] a patriarch: Act.2:29 7:8-9, Heb.7:4.† (AS)

3331.full: περι-άγω [in LXX: Amo.2:10 (הָלַךְ hi.); Isa.28:27, Eze.47:2 (סָבַב hi., ho.); Eze.37:2 46:21 (עָבַר hi), 2Ma.4:38 2Mac 6:10 * ;] __1. to lead about or around: with accusative of person(s), 1Co.9:5. __2. Intrans., to go about: Act.13:11; before ἐν, Mat.4:23; with accusative loc. (governed by the περι-, not so in cl., see Bl., § 34, 1; 53, 1), Mat.9:35 23:15, Mrk.6:6.† (AS)

s: to be better than, superior to
3333.full: 1. to be around a place, with dative, (Thucydides); τὰ περιόντα circumstances , (Demosthenes Orator) 2. to be better than, superior to another, surpass, excel , with genitive, (Iliad by Homer); περίεσσι γυναικῶν εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε (Odyssey by Homer); οἳ περὶ μὲν βουλὴν Δαναῶν περὶ δd ἐστὲ μάχεσθαι λπαρr εθυαλσs μάχην)) (Iliad by Homer); with dative rei, σοφίᾳ π. τῶν Ἑλλήνων (Plato Philosophus): absolute to be superior , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἐκ περιόντος at an advantage , (Thucydides) 3. to overlive, outlive , τινι (Herdotus Historicus): absolute to survive, remain alive , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;of things, to be extant, to be in existence , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. to be over and above, to remain in hand , of property, money, etc., (Thucydides); οἰόμενοι περιεῖναι χρήματά τῳ imagining that any one has a balance in his hands, (Demosthenes Orator) 5. to be a result or consequence , περίεστιν ὑμῖν ἐκ τούτων what you have got by all this is . ., (Demosthenes Orator); τοσοῦτον ὑμῖν περίεστιν τοῦ πρὸς ἐμὲ μίσους you have so much hatred against me left , Philipp. quoted in (Demosthenes Orator); with infinitive, περίεστι ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς ἐρίζειν it remains for you to quarrel with them, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

s: a place for walking, a covered walk
discourse during a walk, a philosophical discussion
3334.full: 1. a walking about, walking , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. a place for walking, a covered walk , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. discourse during a walk, a philosophical discussion , (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. οἱ ἐκ τοῦ περιπάτου the Peripatetics, school of Aristotle , because he taught walking in a περίπατος of the Lyceum at Athens, (Plutarch), etc. (ML)

3335.full: of or from pine or pine-wood , (Sophocles Tragicus); π. δάκρυα tears of the pine , i. e. the resinous drops that ooze from it, (Euripides) (ML)

3336.full: 1. to make fat, fatten , (Euripides); π. χθόνα to fatten the soil, of a dead man, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass. to be or become fat , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. metaphorically, 3. to increase, enlarge , πλοῦτον (Pindar) 4. to make wanton, excite , (Aeschulus Tragicus): —;Pass. to wax fat and wanton , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἔχθεσιν πιαίνεσθαι to batten on quarrels, (Pindar) (ML)

s: desire for advantage, grasping, aggression, cupidity, covetousness
3337.full: πλεονεξία, -ας, ἡ (πλεονέκτης), [in LXX for בֶּצַע ;] the character and conduct of a πλεονέκτης. __1. advantage. __2. desire for advantage, grasping, aggression, cupidity, covetousness: Luk.12:15, Rom.1:29, 2Co.9:5, Eph.4:19 (see ICC, in l) Eph.5:3, Col.3:5, 1Th.2:5, 2Pe.2:3 2:14; pl. (see Bl., § 32, 6), Mrk.7:22.† SYN.: φιλαργυρία, avarice (see Tr., Syn., § xxiv) (AS)

3338.full: 1. to long for, yearn after what is absent, to miss or regret what is lost, Lat. desiderare, (Homer), etc.; ποθεῖς τὸν οὐ παρόντα (Aristophanes Comicus); π. τὰς ἐν τῆι νεότητι ἡδονάς (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass., ὦ ποθουμένη (i.e. Εἰρήνη) (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. of things, to require , ποθεῖ ἡ ἀπόκρισις ἐρώτησιν τοιάνδε (Plato Philosophus) 3. with infinitive to be anxious to do, (Euripides); τὸ νοσοῦν ποθεῖ σε ξυμπαραστάτην λαβεῖν my sickness needs to take thee as an assistant, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. absolute, τὸ ποθοῦν one's desiring, one's longing , (Sophocles Tragicus) 5. as Dep., ποθουμένη φρήν the longing soul, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

3339.full: 1. a marking with various colours, embroidering, embroidery , (Plato Philosophus): in plural pieces of broidery , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. varied aspect, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) 3. versatility, subtlety, craft , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

s: to be a citizen, live as a citizen

3341.full: πραγματία (Rec. -εία, as in cl.), -ας, ἡ (πραγματεύομαι) [in LXX for חֲשַׁל, etc. ;] __1. careful application, hard work. __2. business, occupation: pl., 2Ti.2:4.† (AS)

3342.lxx: in LXX for חוּד, מָרַק, etc.
3342.full: προ-βάλλω [in LXX for חוּד, מָרַק, etc. ;] __1. to throw before. __2. to put forward: with accusative, Act.19:33; of trees, to put forth, produce (sc. φύλλα), Luk.21:30.† (AS)

3343.lxx: in LXX: Dan LXX 11:37 (בִּין), Wis.6:7, al.
3343.full: προ-μοέω, -ῶ and depon. -έομαι, οῦμαι, [in LXX: Dan LXX 11:37 (בִּין), Wis.6:7, al. ;] __1. to foresee. __2. to provide (RV, take thought for): with accusative of thing(s), καλά, Rom.12:17 (-ούμενοι), 2Co.8:21 (-οῦμεν). __3. to provide for (before περί, Wis, l.with): with genitive of person(s), 1Ti.5:8 (-εῖ, WH, mg., -εῖται).† (AS)

3344.full: προ-ΐστημι [in LXX: 2Ki.13:17, Pro.23:5 26:17, Isa.43:24, Amo.6:10 (no proper Heb. equiv.), Dan LXX Bel 1:7, 1Ma.5:19, 4Ma.11:27 * ;] __1. trans. in fut., 1 aor., and mid. 1 aor., to put before, set over (Plat., al.). __2. Intrans., in pf., plpf., 2 aor. and mid. Pres. and impf.; __(a) to preside, rule, govern: Rom.12:8, 1Ti.5:17; with genitive, 1Th.5:12, 1Ti.3:4-5 3:12; __(b) to direct, maintain: with genitive of thing(s), καλῶν ἔργων, Tit.3:8, 14 (on R, mg., profess honest occupations, see CGT, in l; Field, Notes, 223 f.).† (AS)

3345.full: 1. a going or coming to, an approach , ἡ πρ. μάλιστα ταύτῃ ἐγένετο the approach was most feasible on this part, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀπείπατο τὴν πρ. rejected his advances , (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. μελάθρων approach to the halls, (Euripides) 2. an onset , πρόσοδοι τῆς μάχης onsets or attacks , (Euripides) 3. like πομπή II, a solemn procession to a temple with singing and music, (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. the coming forward of a speaker in a public assembly , γράφεσθαι πρόσοδον to petition for a hearing , (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. ποιεῖσθαι πρὸς τὸν δῆμον (Aeschines Orator) 5. income, rent , as opposite to principal, (Demosthenes Orator); often in plural, (Isaeus Orator) 6. of the public revenue, φόρων πρόσοδος (Herdotus Historicus); χρημάτων πρ. (Thucydides); mostly in plural the returns, revenue , Lat. reditus, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

3346.full: 1. to frighten, scare, alarm , Lat. terrere, (Iliad by Homer) 2. intransitive to crouch or cower down for fear (compare πτώσσω), properly of animals, (Sophocles Tragicus); of men, (Pindar), attic; πτ. βωμὸν ὕπο (Euripides); also with accusative loci, πτ. βωμόν to flee cowering to the altar, (Euripides) 3. to crouch like a wild beast ready to spring, (Euripides);—;so of men in ambush, ὑπὸ τεύχεσι πεπτηῶτες (Odyssey by Homer) 4. with accusative rei, to crouch for fear of , ἀπειλάς (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

(RV, all this time), 2Co.12:19.† (AS)

3354.lxx: in LXX for חָשַׁךְ, קָדַר, שָׁחַר
3354.full: σκοτόω, -ῶ (σκότος), [in LXX for חָשַׁךְ, קָדַר, שָׁחַר ;] to darken: Rev.9:2 16:10. Metaphorical, of the mind! pass., Eph.4:18 (cf. σκοτίζω).† (AS)

3358.full: στρατιώτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX; 2Ki.23:8 B1, 2Ma.5:12 2Mac 14:39, III Mac 3:12; 3Ma.3:4 Mac3 * ;] a soldier: Mat.8:9, Mrk.15:16, Jhn.19:2, Act.10:7, al.; metaphorically, σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησ., 2Ti.2:3.† (AS)

3359.full: στρατό-πεδον, -ου, τό (στρατός + πέδον, a plain), [in LXX: Jer.34:1 (חַיִל), 2Ma.8:12, al. ;] __(a) a military camp; __(b) an army: Luk.21:20.† (AS)

3360.full: στράτευμα, -τος, τό (στρατεύω), [in LXX: 1Ma.9:34, 2Ma.5:24 2Mac 8:21 2Mac 12:38 2Mac 13:13; pl., Jdth.11:8, 4Ma.5:1 * ;] __1. = στρατεία (Hdt., al.). __2. an army, a host: pl., Mat.22:7, Rev.9:16 19:14, 19; = soldiers, company of soldiers, Act.23:10, 27; pl., Luk.23:11.† (AS)

to be seized or afflicted by, suffering from
3368.lxx: in LXX for עָצָר, חָבַר, etc.
3368.full: συν-έχω [in LXX for עָצָר, חָבַר, etc. ;] __1. to hold together (τ. συνέχον τ. πάντα, Wis.1:7): of closing the ears, Act.7:57 (τ. στόμα, Isa.52:15); to hem in, press on every side: Luk.8:45 19:43. __2. to hold fast; __(a) of a prisoner, to hold in charge (Luc.; cf. exx. in Deiss., BS, 160; MM, xxiv): Luk.22:63; __(b) to constrain: 2Co.5:14; pass., Luk.12:50, Act.18:5 (τ. λόγῳ; cf. Field, Notes, 128), Php.1:23; in pass., of ills, to be seized or afflicted by, suffering from: Mat.4:24, Luk.4:38 8:37, Act.28:8.† (AS)

3369.lxx: in LXX: Jdg.8:28 11:33 (כָּנַע ni.), Sir.4:31, al.
3369.full: συν-στέλλω (Rec. συσ-), [in LXX: Jdg.8:28 11:33 (כָּנַע ni.), Sir.4:31, al. ;] __1. to draw together, contract, shorten: of time, 1Co.7:29. __2. to wrap up: of enshrouding a body for burial (Eur.), with accusative, Act.5:6.† (AS)

3370.full: 1. vehement, violent, excessive , (Thucydides), etc. 2. of men, violent, impetuous , (Plato Philosophus): also strong, robust , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

3372.lxx: in LXX for אֹדֶם, Exo.28:17, al.; also for שֹׁהַם
3372.full: σάρδιον, -ον, τ [in LXX for אֹדֶם, Exo.28:17, al.; also for שֹׁהַם ;] the sardian stone, sard (of which carnelian is one variety): Rev.4:3 21:20.† (AS)

s: a body of soldiers, a corps
3373.full: 1. a whole compounded of parts, a system , (Plato Philosophus):—; a composition , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. an organised government, constitution , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. a body of soldiers, a corps , (Polybius Historicus) 4. of the Roman Senate, (Plutarch) (ML)

3374.full: in Act., of the woman, to bear children , in Mid., of the man, to beget them , (Xenophon Historicus): in Mid. of both parents, to breed children , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

3375.full: nursing , πόνων τιθηνοὺς ἀποδιδοῦσά σοι τροφάς repaying thee nursing tendance for nursing labours, (Euripides) (ML)

s: to have courage, to venture, dare, be bold
3376.full: τολμάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Job.15:12 (לָקַח), Est.1:18 7:5 (לֵב מָלֵא) Jdth.14:13, 2Ma.4:2, 3Ma.3:21 R, 4Ma.8:18 * ;] to have courage, to venture, dare, be bold: absol, 2Co.11:21; before ἐπί, 2Co.10:2; with inf. (Bl., § 69, 4), Mat.22:46, Mrk.12:34, Luk.20:40, Jhn.21:12, Act.5:13 7:32, Rom.15:18, 1Co.6:1, 2Co.10:12, Php.1:14, Ju 9; to submit to (in cl. usually absol. in this sense), Rom.5:7 (see Field, Notes, 155); τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν, took courage and went in (see Field, op. cit., 44), Mrk.15:43 (cf. ἀπο-τολμάω).† (AS)

3377.full: τραχύς, -εῖα, -ύ [in LXX: Isa.40:4 (רֶכֶס), etc. ;] rough: ὁδοί (Is, l.with), Luk.3:5 (LXX); τοποί (i.e. rocky), Act.27:29.† (AS)

s: the track of a wheel, hence, a track, path
3379.full: τροχιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (τροχός), [in LXX: Pro.2:15 4:11, 26-27 5:6, 21 (מַעְגָּל), Eze.27:19 A* ;] the track of a wheel, hence, a track, path: figuratively, Heb.12:13 (LXX) † (AS)

3380.full: a hole formed by gnawing, a mouse's hole , (Batrachomyomachia) (ML)

3381.full: 1. kingly power, sovereignty , (Pindar), attic; τ. ὑμῶν lordship over you, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. plural, αἱ τυραννίδες, = οἱ τύραννοι, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

3382.lxx: in LXX for שַׁחַת, חֶבֶל, etc.
3382.full: φθορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (φθείρω) [in LXX for שַׁחַת, חֶבֶל, etc. ;] destruction, corruption, decay (see Mayor on 2Pe, App.,175 ff.): Rom.8:21, 1Co.15:42, Col.2:22, 2Pe.2:12; opposite to ζωὴ αἰώνιος, Gal.6:8; by meton., of that which is subject to corruption, 1Co.15:50; of moral decay, 2Pe.1:4 2:12 2:19 (cf. Wis.14:12).† (AS)

s: to shiver, shudder, tremble, from fear
3384.full: φρίσσω (Att.. -ττω, and so 4Ma.14:9 4Mac 17:7) [in LXX: Job.4:15 ( pi.), etc. ;] __1. to be rough, bristle. __2. to shiver, shudder, tremble, from fear: Jas.2:19 (see Hort, in l).† (AS)

3385.lxx: in LXX: Gen.1:14, 16 (מָאוֹר), Dan LXX 12:3 (זֹהַר), I Est.8:79, Wis.13:2, Sir.43:7 *
3385.full: φωστήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ (φῶς), [in LXX: Gen.1:14, 16 (מָאוֹר), Dan LXX 12:3 (זֹהַר), I Est.8:79, Wis.13:2, Sir.43:7 * ;] a luminary, light: Php.2:15, Rev.21:11.† SYN.: φέγγος, φῶς (AS)

3386.full: φάτνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX for אֵבוּס, etc. ;] a manger: Luk.2:7, 12 2:16 13:15 (see DB, iii, 234a, DCG, ii, 111a),† (AS)

3389.full: χειμών, -ῶνος, ὁ [in LXX for גֶּשֶׁם, סְתָו ;] __1. winter: Jhn.10:22, 2Ti.4:21; genitive, χειμῶνος, in winter, Mat.24:20, Mrk.13:18. __2. Prop., a winter storm, hence, generally, a storm, tempest: Mat.16:3 (T, WH, R, mg., om.), Act.27:20.† (AS)

3390.full: 1. to bring into hand, to manage, master, subdue , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. mostly in Mid., to conquer, overpower, subdue , (Herdotus Historicus); so, τήνδ᾽ ἐχειρούμην ἄγραν became master of this booty, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. without any sense of violence, to master, subdue , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 4. χειροῦμαι is also Pass. to be subdued , [variant datesTragica Adespota; future χειρωθήσομαι (Demosthenes Orator); aor1 ἐχειρώθην (Herdotus Historicus); perfect κεχείρωμαι (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

s: the defraying of the cost of the public choruses
3391.full: 1. the office of a χορηγός at Athens, the defraying of the cost of the public choruses , being the chief of the λειτουργίαι, (Thucydides), etc. 2. means for providing χοροί: abundance of means, fortune , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. metaphorically supplies for war , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

3393.full: 1. dry land, land , ἐπὶ χέρσου, opposite to ἐν πόντῳ, (Odyssey by Homer); κύματα κυλινδόμενα προτὶ χέρσον (Odyssey by Homer); κῦμα χέρσῳ ῥηγνύμενον (Iliad by Homer); χέρσῳ on or by land , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. as adjective, χέρσος, ον, dry, firm , of land, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν κονίᾳ χέρσῳ, opposite to πόντῳ, (Pindar) 3. dry, hard, barren , (Herdotus Historicus); χ. λιμήν a harbour left dry , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 4. metaphorically barren, without children , of women, (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive barren of , πυρὰ χέρσος ἀγλαϊσμάτων (Euripides) Prob. from same Root as ξηρός. (ML)

3394.full: 1. an earthen pot, a pot for boiling, pipkin , Lat. olla, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. χύτραι, pots of pulse offered to inferior deities, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

3395.full: ψύχος (LT, ψῦ-, as in cl.), -εος (-ους), τό (ψύχω), [in LXX: Gen.8:22 (קֹר), Job.37:9, Psa.147:17 (קָרָה), Zec.14:6, Dan LXX TH 3:67,69 * ;] cold: Jhn.18:18, Act.28:2, 2Co.11:27.† (AS)

3397.full: ἀθανασία, -ας, ἡ (ἀ-θάνατος, undying; V. MM, VGT, see word), [in LXX: Wis.3:4 4:1 8:13,17 15:3, 4Ma.14:5 16:13 * ;] immortality: 1Co.15:53,54 1Ti.6:16 (cf. Cremer, 285 f.).† (AS)

3398.full: ἀκυρόω, -ῶ (κῦρος, authority), [in LXX: 1Es.6:32 Est.6:1-34, 2Ma.6:1-31 * ;] to revoke, invalidate (MM, VGT, see word): Mat.15:6, Mrk.7:13, Gal.3:17 (Plut.).† (AS)

3399.full: ἀλαζονία(Rec. -εία, the earlier form), -ας, ἡ (ἀλαζών), [in LXX: Wis.5:8 17:7, 2; 4Ma.5:1-38 * ;] the character of an ἀλαζών, boastfulness, vainglory, vaunting: Jas.4:16 (Mayor, in l), 1Jn.2:16.† (AS)
